chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Finding Earl Hines for a club owner
summary: A club owner at 35th and Olive asked Thomas to find Earl Hines, staying at the Grand Central Hotel, to play two or three tunes for him privately for about $100.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Take your money and run. But I'll tell you what he did. He'd bring it back and pay you because Green don't want some to be around any fights, you know. But, there were a great musical incidents that happened. So I went up here to this spot on a Sunday afternoon and the fellow -- I don't know how the first I ran into him. He might have been a-personal fellow there. So he said, "Are you Joe Thomas?" I said, "Yeah, I'm Joe Thomas. Who are you?" HE said, "I'm owner of the place."

NO, this is around 55 and (Grant Graham) Olive, rather. Really around the time when I took my lessons, around 35th and ... So they had a place out there and they had it all draped, all black, you know.

I'd say When they said black, you're the one, baby. So he says to me, "I've heard some talk about you." I said, "Yeah, was it good?" Say, "Yeah but I heard Earl Hines is in town." Earl Hines was doing a similar thing like Louis, like Pops was doing. Come to St. Louis on a Sunday afternoon, Sunday night. Lovely, I'll get back to Louis Armstrong later. And, that's the first time I heard of All Hal Baker. He says he doesn't even remember. I said you've got a tremendous trumpet player like that. So, what happened during this time, Stan, the guy was a tremendous fellow. I don't remember his name but he says, "Do you know Earl Hines?" I said, "No, I don't." "Do you know where he's staying?" I said, "I know where he's staying." Well, in those days, that was the only place you could stay. Have to look for him, he's going to be in one of two places. He said, "Would you find him for me?" I said, "What do you want me to find him for?" He said, "I want him to play a little afternoon for me, like two or three tunes." Well, you know, ... afternoons, he's playing at night. Just two or three tunes, come and play two or three tunes for me.
Well, the guy says, "Do you know where Earl Hines is?" And you say, well, I know he'll be one of two places.

Yeah, and this is a trumpet -- Hal Baker. Never called him Shorty Baker. I thought he was tremendous. And he'd say I like you, too. So, Earl Hines was staying at the Grand Central Hotel. So I got Early -- Early doesn't remember to this day. Went up, one tune. Give me some money for my
trouble. I said, "Well, I can't make any between you and (?). Earl." He said, He made it (?). "Well, have him call me." /... I think it was around $100. He just wanted to hear Earl play.
I see. It was just more or less personal ...
No, no. He had his band there. He wanted Earl Hines a special attraction as his personal.

And the damnedest thingxxxxxxx you think about sequences and that kind of thing, which I sometimes do, he had a place at 35th and Olive m which is right under a place I used to take my lessons. And it was tremendous. St. Louis, at that time, was a tremendous music town and we had some sequences that happened there with me that I was very much surprised about, very much surprised about.
